title: [ORION-QG QG-29] Six-count defect saturation and universal k<=43 affine crossover on TARE scaling rays
body:
Parent programme: #740.
Direct parents: QG-26 #884 / PR #885 guarded finite-template histogram geometry; QG-27 #886 / PR #887 bulk-defect band and exact asymptotic density.
Optional symmetry parent: QG-28 #888 / PR #889 (if GREEN, the same theorem descends from 4096 raw types to 715 local-Clifford orbit counts, but QG-29 does not require it).
Method donors: monotone threshold systems, finite-size scaling, lower envelopes of affine functions, bounded integer defect potentials.

## Status

**PROSPECTIVE FINITE-SIZE SATURATION THEOREM — freeze before execution.**

QG-26 earns

`C_DP(N)=min_{tau feasible}[B_{r(tau)}(N)+K_tau]`

where every active template uses at most six target-column occurrences total and feasibility is only multiplicity guards `N_t >= m_tau(t)`. QG-27 earns the universal template-defect band `-34 <= K_tau <= +8` for relevant optimal/one-active comparison purposes and four distinct bulk baseline forms.

## Q1 — four bulk-class defect potentials

For each distinct bulk baseline form r in `{0,1,2,3}`, define

`kappa_r(N) = min { K_tau : tau has bulk form r and its multiplicity guard is satisfied by N }`.

The exact optimizer becomes

`C_DP(N)=min_r [B_r(N)+kappa_r(N)]`.

A one-active feasible template exists for every valid N and every bulk form, so each kappa_r is finite and `kappa_r(N)<=8`. QG-27 gives `kappa_r(N)>=-34`.

Therefore

`kappa_r(N) in {-34,-33,...,8}`

(43 integer levels).

## Q2 — monotonicity and six-count truncation

If `N' >= N` coordinatewise, every template feasible at N remains feasible at N', hence

`kappa_r(N') <= kappa_r(N)`.

Every template has total active multiplicity <=6. Thus every individual guard threshold satisfies `m_tau(t)<=6`, and template feasibility depends only on the clipped histogram

`clip6(N)_t = min(N_t,6)`.

Therefore

`kappa_r(N)=kappa_r(clip6(N))`.

This is an exact finite-size saturation theorem for the defect term: counts above six affect only the extensive bulk linear forms, never which defect templates are available.

If QG-28 is GREEN, generic/native may additionally state the identical result on 715 orbit counts, but V1 authority must not depend on that optional parent.

## Q3 — bounded number of defect-level changes

Along any coordinatewise nondecreasing histogram path, each integer kappa_r can strictly decrease at most 42 times because it is monotone and lies in the 43-level interval [-34,8].

This bounds **defect-level transitions**, not total optimal-regime switches after competition among the four bulk slopes.

## Q4 — pure scaling rays saturate defect guards by k=6

Fix any valid nonzero integer motif histogram h and `N(k)=k h` for integer `k>=1`.

For every target type with `h_t>0`, `N_t(k)>=6` by k=6. For `h_t=0`, the count is always zero. Since every guard threshold is <=6, every template is either:
- never feasible on the ray; or
- feasible for every k>=6.

Hence each defect potential is exactly constant from k=6 onward:

`kappa_r(kh)=kappa_r^*(h)` for all k>=6.

## Q5 — universal affine-crossover bound k<=43

For k>=6,

`C_DP(kh)=min_r [k*b_r(h)+kappa_r^*(h)]`,

where every slope `b_r(h)=B_r(h)` is an integer and every intercept lies in [-34,8].

Let `b_min=min_r b_r(h)`. If `b_r>b_min`, then the integer slope gap is at least 1. Against any minimal-slope line, the maximum possible intercept advantage is 42. Therefore for every k>=43,

`k*(b_r-b_min) + (kappa_r^* - kappa_min^*) >= 43-42 > 0`.

So no strictly worse bulk slope can remain optimal at k>=43. Among the forms with slope b_min, the smallest stabilized intercept wins/ties forever.

Frozen strong theorem candidate:

> For every valid fixed-matching integer motif histogram h, there exists an exact integer q_h such that
> `C_DP(kh)=k*B_min(h)+q_h` for every integer `k>=43`.

Thus QG-27's eventual-affinity statement admits a **universal grammar-level onset bound 43**, while all template-feasibility changes have already stopped by k=6.

The bound 43 is not claimed sharp.

## Q6 — exact controls

Production and generic ORION must independently bind:
- QG-26 max active occurrences =6 and guard form `N_t>=m_t`;
- QG-27 defect interval [-34,8] and four bulk forms;
- all K/resource quantities are integers;
- one-active template existence for every valid target histogram and every target-permutation/bulk form.

Then machine-enumerate the worst abstract four-line system over:
- integer intercepts in [-34,8];
- integer slopes with `b_min=0` and other gaps in `{0,1,2,3,4,5,6}`;
- all choices of minimal-slope subset;

and require that by k=43 every strictly positive-gap line is dominated, while k=42 is not universally sufficient under the abstract bound (serialize a tight abstract control such as slope gap 1 and intercept advantage -42).

This abstract tightness is only for the **derived bound calculus**, not a claim that a real TARE motif realizes the worst case.

## Native ORION-Q

May authorize:
- `DEFECT_POTENTIAL_CLIP6_SUFFICIENT`;
- `DEFECT_LEVEL_CHANGES_AT_MOST_42_PER_BULK_CLASS`;
- `PURE_SCALING_RAY_DEFECTS_STABLE_BY_K6`;
- `PURE_SCALING_RAY_AFFINE_BY_K43`.

Mandatory false:
- `K43_SHARP_FOR_REAL_TARE`;
- `EXPLICIT_Q_H_FORECASTER`;
- `FINITE_N_GLOBAL_PHASE_BOUNDARY`;
- `CHAIN_ALL_N`;
- `CLOSED_FORM_BDOUBLEPRIME_COMPLETENESS`;
- novelty/R6/physical-advantage authority.

## Intended terminal

`QG29_TARE_DEFECTS_CLIP_AT_6_AND_ALL_SCALING_RAYS_AFFINE_BY_K43_MACHINE_CHECKED`

Honest alternatives: guard-threshold premise refuted; defect-band binding gap; abstract crossover arithmetic refuted; generic/native disagreement; CANNOT_CHECK.

## Donor subtraction

Monotone threshold systems, finite-size scaling and affine-envelope arguments are established donor mathematics. Candidate contribution is only the exact TARE-specific clip-at-six defect theorem and universal k<=43 affine-onset bound.
